title: Plastic problems table
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Making materials (9E); conservation of energy
source: Seeded from science/y9 lesson 12 (Plastic problems table (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 12: Problems with materials. To understand the environmental problems caused by the materials we make and throw away

questions.q: Explain why poly(ethene) lasts so long in the environment.
questions.a: Micro-organisms cannot break down its long chains with strong bonds.
questions.model: Who breaks waste down? Micro-organisms. Can they digest poly(ethene)? No: the long chains with strong carbon bonds are not food for them. So it persists for hundreds of years.

questions.a: Uses land, may leak pollutants, wastes materials.

questions.q: How do microplastics enter food chains?
questions.a: Small animals eat them; predators eat those animals.

questions.q: Core: Make a table of three problems with plastic waste, each with a cause and an effect.
questions.a: For example: ocean litter: careless disposal: animals tangled or eat it.
questions.model: Teacher fills the first row: problem: landfill; cause: plastics do not biodegrade; effect: land used for hundreds of years.

questions.q: Extend: Evaluate bioplastics as a solution (portal response box).
questions.a: For: made from plants, some biodegrade; against: need industrial composting, use farmland; judgement with reason.
Reducing avoids using resources and energy at all; recycling still uses energy and transport.

questions.q: Big question: if plastic is so useful, why is it a problem?
questions.a: It is made from a finite resource and does not biodegrade, so it builds up in land and oceans.
